scope: Independent read-only review of the HRM-013 trusted callback binding carrier, paired Approval waiver bridge, service-binding register, People V61 and Approval V59 candidate manifests, current authority index and both validators.

finalVerdict.reason: All initially reported and follow-up protocol, security, durability, sequence, hash and validator defects are closed. No module source, migration SQL, worktree, runtime, tenant or production authority is granted.

p1Findings: The new service-binding rows described OAuth2 bearer JWT while the endpoint contract forbade Authorization and required X-DWP-Workload-Proof.
The HRM-010 closed claim sets differed between the callback authority and paired Approval bridge.
People V61 had no isolated durable jti and requestNonce replay namespace for HRM-008 through HRM-010.
People V61 lacked the immutable APR-002 request fence and exact-byte durable outbox required by the bridge.
externalReceiptPublicId was not retained in the callback ledger, so FAILED-to-COMPLETED evidence could be overwritten.
The main protocol-fence required values did not match the People V61 callback-authority table.
The callback self digest and originating request or event payload digest were not independently carried and persisted.
Fresh, single-use, audience-bound and purpose-bound step-up evidence could not be enforced by the sealed schemas.
Approval required the decision actor to differ from maker and requester while the People boundary could not independently repeat both checks.
The proposed sequencing attempted to complete APR-002 and HRM-010 before authorizing their bounded People V61 prerequisite persistence.
p2Findings: APR-002 did not have an exact application-header allowlist and deny contract.
Operation identifiers and semantic operation names were not consistently separated across artifacts.
The sealed 16384-byte response limit and persistence limit were not consistently aligned.

closed: Replaced bearer terminology with the exact X-DWP-Workload-Proof certificate-bound RS256 profile and aligned per-binding closed claims.

Added isolated People replay persistence, immutable APR-002 request fence and exact-byte outbox, durable external receipt evidence, separate origin and callback digests, and an exact callback protocol fence.
Added conditional seven-field step-up evidence, maker and requester separation, exact header contracts, operation mappings and response-size constraints.
Changed the next gate to paired Approval V59 and bounded People V61 prerequisite preparation before any HRM-013 owner packet.
followUpFindings: Request byte limits still differed between endpoints and persistence.
Approval grant persistence did not yet provide same-row tenantGrantRevision and authorizationRevision verification.
ownerRevision and decisionRevision equality was not enforced by both database manifests.
The HRM-010 protocol-fence stream did not yet isolate approvalRequestId revision streams.
The standard npm gate did not invoke the dedicated validator, replay identity wording was ambiguous and the dedicated validator repository root was off by one parent.

closed: Aligned every request byte boundary at 32768 bytes and every safe response or receipt boundary at 16384 bytes.
Bound grant_id, tenant_grant_revision and authorization_revision to one current ADMIT row and persisted that identity through request and decision records.
Added typed owner_revision persistence and owner_revision equals decision_revision checks on Approval and People.
Added approval_request_id to the NULLS-NOT-DISTINCT seven-column callback-authority stream key so each waiver request starts and terminates its own revision-one stream.
Defined replay identity as two atomic digest-only rows uniquely keyed by tenant_id and token_digest in both services; raw jti and requestNonce persistence is forbidden.
Connected the dedicated callback validator to the standard npm gate, corrected its repository root and added exact assertions for the previously missed invariants.
Recomputed the current authority index pins after every material correction.

nonClaims: This review does not reserve Approval V59 or People V61.
This review does not authorize source, migration SQL, worktrees, runtime activation, tenant enrollment, production credentials, production binding or release.
This review does not authorize the HRM-013 module owner packet or claim HRM-013, Batch-06 or HRIS completion.
